clue.text: Huge business in the theatre

definitions.meaning: a vast commercial group run by one tycoon
the name of many British music halls and theatres, such as the one in Leicester Square

explanation.surface: A big company operating inside a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprawling business group is called a commercial empire, and the Empire is a classic name for a variety theatre in Britain.

clue.text: Import a dish of pies and mash

indicators.note: a dish is a mixture served up, so these letters are tossed together into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone imports a plate of pies with mashed potato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Import' looks like a verb about trade, but it is the noun meaning significance.
explanation.definitionFit: Import as a noun means importance or stress, which is what special weight or significance placed on something is.

clue.text: Hardly an ungainly type

parts.note: read 'ungainly' as un-gain-ly, someone without gain; the person meant is the very opposite, always making money

explanation.surface: This person is anything but clumsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer who makes excessive gains is the opposite of someone lacking gain.

clue.text: Excellent yet not well done

definitions.meaning: cooked lightly, as a steak can be

explanation.surface: Something is superb yet undercooked, like a good steak.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare means exceptionally good, and also describes meat cooked only briefly.

clue.text: Unwelcome on a ship they're accepted at school

definitions.meaning: pirates or attackers who climb onto a vessel
pupils who live in at a residential school

explanation.surface: People unwanted aboard a vessel are welcomed at a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiders who storm a ship and pupils living in at school share the same name, from boarding.

clue.text: Prospect following land clearance

parts.note: the view a sailor gets once the coast is cleared and left behind: water all round

explanation.surface: A view revealed after ground has been cleared of trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land clearance' suggests clearing a site; read it as a ship clearing the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Once a ship has cleared land, the prospect or view ahead is unbroken ocean away from the coast.

clue.text: Call the boss -he'll crack the whip!

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
a master is someone in charge

explanation.surface: Phone your manager, who will be strict!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack the whip' sounds like strict management, but the circus whip is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: In a circus the man in charge of the ring cracks a whip to direct the performers.

clue.text: One flies right away from remorse

indicators.note: something taken away from a word is removed from it, so this letter goes from the synonym

parts.note: regret is a feeling of remorse

explanation.surface: Someone escapes swiftly from their feelings of guilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' looks like a verb of escape; it is the bird's action.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron-like wading bird is one example of a creature that flies.

clue.text: Boil, or the spot on top

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece on top comes first, so this one is written above the next

parts.note: to spot something is to see it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boil, or perhaps the pimple at its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spot' looks like a pimple to go with 'Boil', but it is the verb meaning notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To bubble violently, like water at boiling point, is another word for boiling.

clue.text: Wrongly blamed for having dawdled

indicators.note: the letters are arranged wrongly, so they must be reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone was unfairly blamed for being slow.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk at a slow leisurely pace is to stroll, so having strolled is having dawdled.

clue.text: A plan for putting on weight

indicators.note: one piece is put on, added after, the other

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a gramme is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A diet scheme designed to make someone gain weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule of planned activities or events is a plan of action.

clue.text: It conveys a sense of courage

definitions.meaning: a fibre carrying signals of touch, sight and so on to the brain

explanation.surface: Something transmits a feeling of bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: A fibre carrying sensation is a nerve, and nerve also means boldness or daring.

clue.text: Opening requires a key, it is needed to succeed

indicators.note: to succeed is to come after, so this piece follows the others

parts.note: D is a musical key
taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting in requires a key, which you need to get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeed' reads as win; here it means follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal entrance into a mine is an opening in the hillside.

clue.text: Draw stumps in an evenly contested game

definitions.meaning: in cricket, pulling up the stumps ends play, so it means finish the game
a contest where the sides are nearly level

explanation.surface: Play finishes in a tight cricket contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: the umpires pull out the stumps (the wickets) to end a day's play.
explanation.definitionFit: To end a game is to close the fixture, and a tight contest is also called a near-level fixture.

clue.text: Wolf, say, or a beast of burden

definitions.meaning: a wolf is an example of a creature that hunts in a group
a mule or donkey carrying loads

explanation.surface: A wolf, or perhaps a donkey laden with goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolves live in packs, and a load-carrying mule is also named after the packs it carries.

clue.text: Country music composer

definitions.meaning: John ..., an English composer of the early twentieth century

explanation.surface: Someone who writes country and western songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country music' looks like one phrase; split it after 'Country'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eire is a nation, and John Ireland was an English composer of songs and piano music.

clue.text: Seal is broken, revealing passages

indicators.note: something broken has its parts out of place, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seal is broken open to reveal hidden corridors.
explanation.definitionFit: Walkways between rows of seats or shelves are passages.

clue.text: Passed over for dead, for example?

definitions.text: Passed over for dead, for example?

parts.words: Passed over for dead, for example?
parts.note: 'passed over' used in place of 'dead' is a gentle substitute expression; the clue gives an example of the device

explanation.surface: Someone was overlooked because they were thought to have died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed over' looks like being ignored; read it as the polite phrase for having died.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild expression replacing a harsh one, like 'passed over' for died, is this figure of speech.

clue.text: It was instrumental in combining rest and play

indicators.note: when things are combined they are mixed up together, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something helped in balancing relaxation and amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrumental' looks like 'helpful'; it means it was a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient stringed instrument plucked like a zither, so it was literally an instrument.

clue.text: Middleman gets even more in debt

definitions.meaning: an agent who arranges deals between buyers and sellers

explanation.surface: The agent ends up with still bigger debts.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent arranging deals is a go-between, and someone more penniless than another is more broke.

clue.text: Adjusting, freeing and gathering up sails

indicators.note: adjusting something rearranges it, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor adjusts, frees and furls the canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking in sail by rolling or tying part of it is the nautical term for reducing canvas.

clue.text: They're flat but suitable for climbers, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the word is replaced by one pronounced the same

parts.note: steps are for climbing up

explanation.surface: Some land is level, but still good for mountaineers apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Vast treeless grassy plains of Russia and Central Asia are flat land.

clue.text: Thus material comfort results

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
lace is a delicate fabric

explanation.surface: Accordingly, cosy fabric is the outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Consolation given in grief is comfort.

clue.text: Result of running repair

parts.note: a sharp pain in the side caused by running, or the result of sewing a quick running repair

explanation.surface: What a hurried mending job produces.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop of thread from sewing, and a sharp side pain from running, share the same name.

clue.text: Dance with Jack before everyone retires

parts.note: Jack and tar are both slang for a sailor
ante is Latin for before

indicators.note: something that retires goes back, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A sailor dances until the whole party heads off to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapid whirling folk dance from southern Italy.

clue.text: Moving arm up and down

indicators.note: in a down entry the word reads the same going up as going down

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A limb swinging up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating part of a machine, such as a helicopter blade, is an arm that moves round.

clue.text: Take off a ring, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is pronounced, so the word is swapped for one that sounds the same

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells

explanation.surface: Removing a wedding band, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip off a skin or outer layer is to take it off.

clue.text: A love for indigo

parts.note: love is a zero score in tennis, so nil

explanation.surface: Someone has a passion for a deep blue colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A West Indian shrub yielding blue dye, and that dye, is indigo.

clue.text: Image to carry to top of mountain

parts.note: to tote is to carry

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A picture to be carried up to the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved emblem revered by a clan is a sacred image.

clue.text: In money I've a reason for working

parts.note: taken as written
a cent is a coin, a unit of money
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: With cash, I have a motive to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A motivation that drives someone to work, such as a bonus.

clue.text: If you study it you may become an expert in time

definitions.text: If you study it you may become an expert in time

parts.words: If you study it you may become an expert in time
parts.note: reads as 'eventually you will master it' but means mastering the subject of clocks and timekeeping

explanation.surface: With study, mastery comes eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of measuring time and making clocks makes one a timekeeping expert.

clue.text: Fragile copy

definitions.meaning: a thin carbon copy on light paper, journalists' slang

explanation.surface: A delicate duplicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Insubstantial things are fragile, and thin carbon paper copies were once called by the same name.
